To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
collaboration with universities and institutes via a technology company is the most effective in building innovation capability.

the collaboration with universities via an intermediary organization facilitates the ambidexterity of the SMEs, but the intermediary organization should be a wholly owned or joint-venture technology company, not a technology department or a research centre.

the collaboration with universities or research institutes facilitates both the exploratory and the exploitative types of capability building, but the collaboration via a ‘department’ is the least (and via a joint-ventured ‘company’ is the most) effective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of organizational forms in response and adaptation to external collaboration, which is a critical issue that has received limited attention in the literature.
how the organizational forms of external collaboration affect innovation capability building, and the implications for innovation capability building through intermediary organization.
a new type of intermediary organization that is created and developed by SMEs to facilitate their innovation capability building.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the organizational forms of SMEs' technology departments, research centres and technology companies have evolved in response to the external collaboration with universities and R&D institutes.
the evolution of the organizational forms in response of external collaboration facilitates the building of the SMEs’ innovation capability.

the collaboration via a ‘quasiintermediary organization’ is most effective for the exploratory type, while the collaboration via a fully independent ‘technology company’ is most effective to facilitate both the exploratory and exploitor types of innovation capability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the context of SMEs' innovation capability building, a joint venture between SMEs and universities and research institutes can help to build an intermediary organization, which can facilitate both exploratory and exploratory types of innovation capability.

, in general, SMEs can effectively leverage their external collaborations with universities and research institutions to build their innovation capabilities through intermediary organizations, which are the ‘technology department’, ‘research centre’, and ‘technology company’.
the collaboration with universities via a ‘technology company’ is the most effective for building an ambidextrous type of innovation capability.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the SMEs' innovation capability building can be facilitated by the evolution of the organizational forms of the intermediary organizations, and the SMEs' organizational forms of the technology department, research centre or technology company can be viewed as an important organizational mechanism to facilitate their external collaboration with universities and institutes.
the organizational forms in response the collaboration with universities or research institutes are critical for building the innovation capability of manufacturing SMEs.

the evolution of an intermediary organizational form is a critical strategy for organizations in building their innovation capability, and the evolution process can be facilitated through collaboration with universities and/or research institutes.
